candidates.rationale: Warns that waiting for perfect conditions means nothing ever gets done.
Paul admits he hasn't attained perfection yet but presses on, modeling progress over flawlessness.
God's strength is made perfect in weakness, affirming that our imperfections are where grace operates.
Paul acknowledges the gap between intention and execution, normalizing our inability to achieve perfection.
Cautions against being overly righteous or wise, suggesting that perfectionism can be self-destructive.
